newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-China Industrial unit offer effective.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-China Industrial unit offer effective.

text.p: U.S.-China Industrial Exchange Inc said Tuesday the Securities and Exchange Commission has declared effective its registration statement for a $10 million underwritten public offering.
The registration applies to 10,000 "new units" priced at $1,000 each, the company said. The offering also includes an option for 1,500 new units to cover over-allotments.

Each new unit consists of 255 original units, which were issued in the company's initial public offering in August 1994. These units consist of one share of common stock, one redeemable Class A Warrant and one redeemable Class B Warrant, the company said.
Executive Vice President Lawrence Pemble said he believes all units should sell Tuesday. The offer raises the company's outstanding units from 3.84 million to about 5.94, Pemble said.
U.S.-China Industrial Exchange was trading around 4-3/4 Tuesday, up from 3-7/8 at Monday's close.

U.S.-China Industrial Exchange Inc was founded in 1981 and represents Western manufacturers in China in making and marketing their products. It is also the 90 percent owner of a women's and children's health clinic in China, Pemble said.
